title: Export the model to an IFC file and publish it
task: Export the whole document to IFC with Document.Export + IFCExportOptions inside a transaction, writing into the connector's ExportsDirectory, then Connector.Publish the .ifc so the caller can fetch it. Covers IFC export, its transaction requirement (the opposite of DWG export), and file publishing.

pitfalls.symptom: doc.Export(folder, name, new IFCExportOptions()) called at top level (between blocks) fails with connector code script-write-outside-transaction / Autodesk ModificationOutsideTransactionException 'Modifying is forbidden because the document has no open transaction'.
pitfalls.cause: The IFC exporter writes temporary data into the document during export, so it requires an ambient transaction — the OPPOSITE of DWG export (Document.Export with DWGExportOptions), which manages its own transaction and must be called with none open.
pitfalls.fix: Call the IFC Document.Export overload INSIDE a Connector.WithTransaction(doc, () => { ... }) block. It leaves no net element change (the transaction only satisfies the exporter's requirement); the file itself comes back via Connector.Publish, not via the model.

pitfalls.symptom: The IFC file is written but the caller cannot retrieve it (it lands in a temp folder on the Revit machine).
pitfalls.cause: Document.Export only writes a file on disk; nothing returns it to the agent unless it is published from the connector's exchange workspace.
pitfalls.fix: Export into Connector.ExportsDirectory and call Connector.Publish(path) on the written file, exactly as the DWG export how-to does; the published file appears in the result's files[].

pitfalls.symptom: A task-phrased search like 'export the model to an IFC file' does not surface the export method; top hits are Application.ExportIFCCategoryTable and IFCExportOptions properties.
pitfalls.cause: Document.Export(string folder, string name, IFCExportOptions options) ranks poorly for IFC intent (connector issue #341); PDF export by contrast surfaces at rank 3.
pitfalls.fix: Search naming the member, e.g. 'Document.Export the model to an IFC file with IFCExportOptions' (returns the correct overload at rank 1).
